phases.phase: B3 — Launch-tier sheriff scrapers (JSO, OCFL, PBSO)
phases.goal: Build the three lowest-friction scrapers first. These exercise the full pipeline end-to-end with the lowest captcha risk, so we hit the matcher integration with real production rows in <2 weeks of wall-clock.
deliverables: OCFL scraper (`lib/scrapers/vendors/ocfl-bestjail.ts`) — built first because it's the easiest probe (effort=4h). Strategy: 30-min cron fetches `/BestJail/PDF/bookings.pdf`, parses booking numbers with pdf-parse, diffs against InmateBooking, then enriches new ones via getInmateDetails + getCharges. NEVER enumerate A-Z. Mugshot bytes are stripped before parse (privacy filter).

PBSO scraper (`lib/scrapers/vendors/pbso-blotter.ts`) — daily 6am cron, stealth-chromium navigates to /blotter/, POSTs 2-day rolling start/end window, pages through results, parses `Name:` anchor-delimited blocks via the regex spec. Detects hCaptcha presence and halts+alerts ops if hCaptcha becomes enforced. Build hours: 7.

JSO scraper (`lib/scrapers/vendors/jso-bookings.ts`) — hourly cron with reCAPTCHA v2 solver (Bright Data Web Unlocker built-in solver primary, 2Captcha fallback). Captures auth token once per session, batches RecentBookings + ReleaseLog within token TTL (cuts captcha spend in half). Build hours: 14. Confirms `bookingDate` field name on first live solve (per OpenQuestion in matcher design).
Wire all three into `lib/cron/discovery/` and `lib/cron/worker.ts` dispatch map (`scrapeJsoBookings`, `scrapeOcflBestjail`, `scrapePbsoBlotter`).

// =============================================================================
// JAIL / INMATE BOOKINGS — Option B freshness-layer signal
// APPEND TO prisma/schema.prisma in the "FRESHNESS LAYER / SCRAPE DATA" zone,
// right after model Foreclosure. Zero ALTERs to existing tables.
// =============================================================================

model InmateBooking {
  id                    String   @id @default(cuid())

  // Source identity
  sheriffSlug           String   // "jso" | "hcso" | "ocfl" | "bso" | "mdcr" | "pbso"
  countyFips            String   // "12031" | "12057" | "12095" | "12011" | "12086" | "12099"
  state                 String   @default("FL")

  // Booking identifiers (varies by sheriff — coerced to string)
  bookingId             String   // canonical PK component
  externalBookingNo     String?
  incarcerationId       String?  // JSO-only
  inmateNumber          String?  // person-stable where exposed
  jacketNumber          String?  // PBSO person-stable
  obtsNumber            String?  // statewide FDLE OBTS — cross-county join key
  idsNumber             String?  // MDCR internal person ID

  // Person identity
  fullName              String
  firstName             String?
  middleName            String?
  lastName              String?
  suffix                String?
  normalizedName        String   // see normalizeInmateName spec
  dateOfBirth           DateTime?
  age                   Int?     // when DOB suppressed (OCFL exposes age only)
  race                  String?
  gender                String?
  height                String?
  weight                String?
  eyeColor              String?
  hairColor             String?

  // Booking event
  bookingDate           DateTime
  releaseDate           DateTime?
  bookingFacility       String?
  cellLocation          String?
  arrestingAgency       String?
  arrestType            String?
  holdsForOtherAgencies Boolean?
  immigrationHold       Boolean?

  // Charges + bond (denormalized for fast filter, raw kept as JSON)
  charges               Json
  chargeCount           Int      @default(0)
  topChargeStatute      String?
  topChargeDesc         String?
  topChargeSeverity     String?  // FT|FF|FS|MF|MS|CT|null

  totalBond             Int?     // CENTS
  highestSingleBond     Int?     // CENTS
  bondType              String?  // see bond-taxonomy
  isNoBond              Boolean  @default(false)

  courtDate             DateTime?
  courtLocation         String?
  courtDepartment       String?

  // Address (rare — OCFL only)
  addressStreet         String?
  addressApt            String?
  addressCity           String?
  addressState          String?
  addressZip            String?

  // Mugshot (pointer-only — bytes in R2; feature-flagged OFF in v1)
  mugshotUrl            String?
  mugshotStorageKey     String?
  mugshotCapturedAt     DateTime?

  // Matcher state (written by jail-parcel-matcher.ts, NOT scraper)
  parcelId              String?
  matchConfidence       Float?
  matchMethod           String?  // S1_NAME_DOB | S2_FULLKEY | S3_UNIQUE_COUNTY | S4_CITY | S5_HOMESTEAD | S6_FUZZY | S7_HYPHEN | MANUAL
  matchStatus           String?  // BOUND | PROVISIONAL | AMBIGUOUS | NO_MATCH | SUPPRESSED | MANUAL
  candidateParcelIds    Json?    // up to 5 candidates when AMBIGUOUS
  matchedAt             DateTime?

  // §119.071 exempt handling (defense-in-depth)
  isExempt              Boolean  @default(false)
  exemptReason          String?
  exemptAt              DateTime?
  suppressed            Boolean  @default(false) // right-to-be-forgotten

  // Provenance (mirrors ParcelSale / RawSnapshot)
  source                String
  sourceTag             String?
  legalRisk             String   @default("yellow")
  capturedAt            DateTime @default(now())
  lastSeenAt            DateTime @default(now())
  rawSnapshotId         String?

  createdAt             DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime @updatedAt

  matchLogs             JailBookingMatchLog[]

  // Idempotent re-scrape — (sheriffSlug, bookingId) unique across all 6 sources
  @@unique([sheriffSlug, bookingId])

  // Matcher hot paths
  @@index([normalizedName, countyFips])
  @@index([countyFips, bookingDate])
  @@index([parcelId])
  @@index([dateOfBirth])
  @@index([obtsNumber])

  // Analytics / freshness
  @@index([sheriffSlug, capturedAt])
  @@index([releaseDate])
  @@index([legalRisk])
  @@index([isExempt])
  @@index([suppressed])
  @@index([bookingDate])
}

// Audit trail: every match decision (Tier-1 onScrape, Tier-2 nightly, Tier-3 ParcelSale).
// Lets us answer "why was this booking bound to that parcel" 6 months later, and
// safely re-run matcher logic by replaying logs.
model JailBookingMatchLog {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  bookingId       String
  inmateBooking   InmateBooking @relation(fields: [bookingId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  parcelId        String?  // null when AMBIGUOUS / NO_MATCH
  strategy        String   // S1_NAME_DOB ... S7_HYPHEN | REJECT_AMBIGUOUS
  confidence      Float?
  candidateCount  Int      @default(0)
  matchStatus     String   // BOUND | PROVISIONAL | AMBIGUOUS | NO_MATCH | SUPPRESSED | MANUAL
  matcherVersion  String   // e.g. "v1.0"
  triggeredBy     String   // "onScrape" | "nightlyReconcile" | "onParcelSale" | "manualBackfill"
  batchId         String?
  matchedByUserId String?  // for MANUAL bindings
  notes           String?  @db.Text
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([bookingId])
  @@index([parcelId])
  @@index([strategy])
  @@index([batchId])
  @@index([createdAt])
}

// Defense-in-depth §119.071 / Marsy's Law filter. Hard-blocks scoring for any
// name in this list even if the sheriff site leaked it. Seeded weekly from
// FDLE-published exempt-categories, FL Bar judicial roll, FL prosecutors'
// association roster, and manual ops additions.
model ExemptOccupationDictionary {
  id                 String   @id @default(cuid())
  normalizedName     String                                   // pre-normalized for fast join
  fullName           String                                   // raw display
  occupationCategory String                                   // "LEO" | "JUDGE" | "PROSECUTOR" | "VICTIM" | "WITNESS" | "OTHER"
  sourceFeed         String                                   // "FDLE_exempt_categories" | "FL_bar_judicial" | "ops_manual" ...
  lastVerifiedAt     DateTime @default(now())
  active             Boolean  @default(true)
  notes              String?

  createdAt          DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt          DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([normalizedName])
  @@index([occupationCategory])
  @@index([active])
}

verdict.refutationReasoning:
This plan has substantive gaps across schema, matcher correctness, aggregation semantics, privacy, integration, and effort estimation. Default posture (gaps until proven otherwise) holds.

## 1. SCHEMA GAPS (verified against prisma/schema.prisma)

**1a. Parcel-side index for the matcher does not exist and is not being added.** The plan only adds a trigram GIN on `Parcel.ownerName` for S6, but S1/S2/S3/S4/S5/S7 all do `findMany({ where: { countyFips, ownerName: { not: null } } })` then filter in Node. The actual `Parcel` table (lines 1647–1693) carries 10.998M FL rows; Orange alone is ~510k. S1's `prisma.parcel.findMany({ where: { countyFips, ownerName: { not: null } } })` will pull ~500k rows per booking into Node memory and run JS filter. For ~175 OCFL bookings/day × ~510k Orange parcels = ~90M cross-product per run. Plan's claim "<30s wall-clock" is unsupported. Required: a normalized owner-name column on Parcel (`ownerNameNormalized`) and a `(countyFips, ownerNameNormalized)` btree index, or move every strategy to pg_trgm `%` search like S6. The plan's "denormalized matcher-side index lives on InmateBooking" sentence does NOT solve this — the parcel-side index is the bottleneck.

**1b. No `ownerCorporate` boolean on Parcel.** `parseOwnerName` is called per-row inside `isNonCorporateNameMatch` filter, which is fine at small scale but runs ~510k times per booking with no caching. There is no `ownerCorporate` denormalized column and no plan to backfill it. This is both a perf issue and an LLC-trap issue (see 2a).

**1c. `ParcelSale` model already exists (line 1617). Plan's "Tier-3 (onParcelSale) deferred to v1.1" leaves a documented hole**: when ownership changes via ParcelSale, BOUND InmateBookings will continue to point at the old owner's parcel until nightly reconcile re-matches by name. If old owner kept the name match (common), the booking stays bound to a parcel they no longer own. No invalidation on Parcel.ownerName change.

**1d. JailBookingMatchLog has no cap or retention policy.** Every booking gets a log row on every Tier-1 + Tier-2 + future Tier-3 pass. With reconcile rerunning across a trailing 30-day window nightly, a single booking accumulates ~30 log rows in its first month. At 3 launch sources × ~150 bookings/day × 30 days = ~135k log rows/month minimum, plus exponential growth at v1.5. No retention cron mentioned.

**1e. `candidateParcelIds Json?` violates referential integrity.** Stored as JSON string array — no FK, no cascade delete when Parcel is removed. Plus Prisma JSON field cannot be queried by element with the indexes the plan adds. Should be a join table (`InmateBookingCandidateParcel`).

**1f. `obtsNumber` is collected (PBSO) but never used as a matching key.** Plan calls it "statewide FDLE OBTS — cross-county join key" in the schema comment but the matcher S1–S7 strategies never check `WHERE obtsNumber = ?` against existing InmateBooking rows. Recidivism counting across counties is broken — same person booked in Duval and Hillsborough counts as two distinct people for the RECIDIVISM_MULTIPLE_BOOKINGS_12MO signal.

## 2. MATCHER GAPS

**2a. Joint-tenant / married-couple owners produce false negatives, not false positives.** Typical FL ownerName: `"SMITH JOHN A & MARY"` or `"SMITH JOHN A & SMITH MARY"`. Plan's `parseOwnerName` is described as outputting `{ ownerCorporate, candidates: NormalizedName[] }` but the matcher's `isNonCorporateNameMatch` checks `candidates.some(c => c.nameKey === inmateNorm)` — fine, but a trigram GIN on raw `ownerName` (column literally being indexed) will return low similarity for `"SMITH JOHN A & MARY"` vs inmate normalized `"JOHN SMITH"`. S6 will silently miss most joint-tenant matches. Plan needs to ALSO index the normalized candidate strings, which means a separate table OR a `ownerNameNormalizedSet text[]` column.

**2b. Common-name false positives at S3.** Plan says S3 fires when `nameKey` exact + unique-in-county. In Miami-Dade (~870k parcels), `JOSE GARCIA` likely appears as primary owner on 50+ parcels. S3 will fire ZERO times on those, which is good. But "JAVIER MARTINEZ JR" with a suffix — if there's exactly one in the county he might own a $300k house OR the inmate might be his cousin. S3 returns confidence 0.80 (above 0.78 floor) → BOUND. No DOB on Parcel means S1 silently degrades to "name exact + unique" (the schema delta admits this: "S1 effectively requires DOB on inmate side and reduces to name exact + unique"). At that point S1 and S3 are the same query with different confidences — S1=0.97, S3=0.80. The strategy ladder is essentially broken: S1 will fire identically to S3 but with falsely-inflated confidence. This is a precision-killer.

**2c. Hispanic surname compounds.** Miami-Dade is 68% Hispanic per the inventory notes for MDCR. Typical inmate name from MDCR: `GARCIA-LOPEZ JUAN CARLOS`. Plan's S7 hyphen split tries `JUAN GARCIA` and `JUAN LOPEZ` against parcel `ownerName`. But the parcel owner may be `GARCIA JUAN CARLOS` or `LOPEZ GARCIA JUAN C` or — most commonly — the maternal surname comes first (LOPEZ). The matcher has no FL-Hispanic-name handling beyond a naive split. Will both miss real matches AND falsely bind to neighbors with similar surnames.

**2d. S5 homestead heuristic is wrong.** Plan says S5 = "situsAddress == ownerMailingAddress". Many FL homestead-exempt properties have the owner's mailing address as a PO box or a separate residence; the homestead exemption is recorded as a tax-roll flag (`EXMPT_TYP_01 = '01'`), NOT inferred from address equality. The schema does not appear to capture HX_FLAG. S5 will both miss true homesteads (PO box mailing) AND falsely bind to investor-owned properties where the owner happens to use the situs as mailing for accounting reasons.

**2e. Sticky MANUAL bindings + ParcelSale = phantom bonds.** After an analyst manually binds Booking-A → Parcel-X, the matcher never re-evaluates. If Parcel-X sells (ParcelSale row appears, ownerName changes), Booking-A is still bound. The investor sees "Liquidity Pressure +22" on a property whose owner has nothing to do with the booking. There is NO ParcelSale-triggered invalidation even for MANUAL bindings.

**2f. The matcher per-booking N+1 pattern.** `matchJailBookingBatch` calls `matchOne(booking)` in a serial `for` loop. Each `matchOne` issues 6–7 Postgres queries. For nightly reconcile at 30-day window × 3 sources × ~150/day ≈ 13.5k bookings × 6 queries = ~80k queries minimum. At Railway's connection-pool of 15 this serializes. "Wall-clock <2 min" is unsupported.

## 3. AGGREGATION GAPS

**3a. Mutual-exclusivity bug between ACTIVE and POSTED across separate bookings.** The check `if (jailContext.activeBondInCustody) ... else if (jailContext.postedBondDate)` only considers the latest single booking (lead query takes `take: 1`). But suppose:
- Booking A: 30 days ago, released — POSTED_CASH_BOND_RECENT +15
- Booking B: 2 days ago, in custody — ACTIVE_BOND_IN_CUSTODY +22

The Leads route orders `[{ releaseDate: 'asc' }, { bookingDate: 'desc' }]`. `releaseDate: 'asc'` with NULLS LAST in Postgres puts the in-custody booking SECOND (NULL sorts last in ASC). So `take: 1` returns the RELEASED booking and the investor sees +15 when they should see +22. Either reverse the order to `releaseDate: 'asc' NULLS FIRST` (which Prisma cannot express directly — requires raw SQL or `releaseDate: 'desc'` with manual reordering) or fetch top-3 and pick in code.

**3b. RECIDIVISM count is hand-waved.** The integration code comment says `bookingCount12mo: /* computed via separate aggregation, or 1 */ 1`. Hardcoding to 1 disables the entire RECIDIVISM signal. No plan deliverable specifies the SQL aggregate. Adds B4-equivalent effort that isn't budgeted.

**3c. Decay function double-counts when both ACTIVE and HIGH_BOND stack.** Plan applies decay to ACTIVE (22 × decay) and to HIGH_BOND (5 × decay) separately. But HIGH_BOND is a modifier of the same event — the decay is being applied twice to the same liquidity event. Either decay applies once to the whole jail-channel sum, or HIGH_BOND should be undecayed. Either way, the math as written is conceptually doubled.

**3d. 30-pt cap is computed BEFORE adding to totalScore but RECIDIVISM is added undecayed.** The recidivism +8 is added without decay regardless of last event age. A 700-day-old recidivism signal contributes the full +8 even though all individual bookings are deep in REGIME D. Tooltip for investors will show "Recurring Pressure: +8" with no obvious recency.

**3e. matchConfidence FLOOR is inconsistent.** Plan says `MATCH_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.78` in the aggregation integration; says `HIGH_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.85` and `PROVISIONAL_FLOOR = 0.50` in the matcher; says `parcelId = confidenceMeetsFloor ? r.parcelId : null` where `confidenceMeetsFloor = r.confidence >= 0.78`. So `S3_UNIQUE_COUNTY` at 0.80 confidence will write `parcelId` populated AND status=BOUND. But the matcher also writes status=PROVISIONAL for S4 at 0.72 — below 0.78 — yet that's marked `status='PROVISIONAL'`, not 'NO_MATCH'. The leads route filters by `matchConfidence >= 0.78`, so PROVISIONAL rows with parcelId NULL but confidence 0.72 will silently disappear. Then the aggregation `jailContext.matchConfidence < 0.78 → 0 contribution` path is unreachable because the row was already filtered upstream. The defense-in-depth is meaningless and the floor is enforced in 3 different places with overlapping logic.

## 4. PRIVACY GAPS

**4a. CI test for neutral-copy audit is mentioned in privacyChecklist (#10) but NOT in any phase deliverable.** Without it the regex audit is a one-time check, not a CI gate. Easy to drift.

**4b. RawSnapshot leakage.** Plan says scrapers write to `RawSnapshot` with `legalRisk='yellow'` and `rawResponse` = the full JSON payload — which includes charges, mugshot URLs, full names. Any developer with database read access has the full raw arrest record indefinitely. The "one SQL purge" capability is only useful if you receive a cease-and-desist; it does nothing to limit internal access. No row-level security policy or column encryption proposed.

**4c. Mugshot bytes 'stripped before parse' (privacyChecklist #15) but the OCFL plan says 'STRIP mugshot base64 BEFORE parse'. The actual scraper code is not written; this is a TODO that depends on parsing the PDF byte stream correctly. If pdf-parse is used naively, mugshot base64 strings will land in `RawSnapshot.rawResponse` despite the stated intent. No test fixture verifies absence of base64 from RawSnapshot.

**4d. Juvenile exclusion (privacyChecklist #4) lacks a mechanism for DOB-suppressed sources.** OCFL exposes age only; JSO has neither DOB nor age. "Min-age heuristic for DOB-suppressed sources" is hand-waved — there is no enforceable rule for JSO. A juvenile booking from JSO could flow through unblocked.

**4e. ExemptOccupationDictionary 'normalizedName' join collides.** Common names will false-positive the suppression filter. Example: an actual exempt LEO named "JOHN SMITH" in the dictionary will block EVERY booking with normalizedName "JOHN SMITH" statewide — including legitimate non-LEO arrestees. Defense-in-depth turns into a precision-destroying false-suppression. The dictionary needs to be name+DOB+jurisdiction-scoped, not name-only.

**4f. Marsy's Law victim-suppression for chapter 741/784/794/800/827 charges (privacyChecklist #2)** is mentioned but not implemented. Charges are stored as JSON; the suppression logic has no place in B4 deliverables and is not wired into the aggregation. Will silently fail to suppress.

## 5. PER-SHERIFF SCRAPER GAPS

**5a. ScrapeRegistry dispatch is registered by `sourceKey`, not by `scraperFn`** (verified at `lib/scrapers/dispatch/index.ts`). The DISPATCH map is `Record<sourceKey, ScraperAdapter>`. The plan's B3 deliverable says "add 3 entries to dispatch map" with `scraperFn` names like `scrapeJsoBookings` — but the dispatch map is keyed by sourceKey strings like `"jso-jail-bookings"`. jso.summary: JSO publishes the inmate roster at https://inmatesearch.jaxsheriff.org/ — an Angular SPA that calls a JSON API at https://inmatesearch-api.jaxsheriff.org:8443/. The API is gated by an invisible reCAPTCHA v2 (siteKey 6LeN5c8iAAAAANQZxRPp9ei_ZPTGZvCKw_1rZU_6, UseCaptcha:true in /assets/config.json). The Angular client posts the recaptcha token to GET /Captcha/GetCaptchaResponse?captchaResponse=<token>, the server returns an opaque auth token that is then sent as the `Authorization` header on every /search/* call. Without a valid recaptcha solve, the API returns 401. There is NO Cloudflare/Akamai/IP block — the only friction is the captcha. The key endpoint for freshness scraping is GET /search/RecentBookings?timediff=<hours>, which is purpose-built for "what booked in the last N hours" — exactly our use case. /search/ReleaseLog?timediff=<hours> gives the release-side delta. /search/InmateDetails?incarcerationId=<id> is the per-row drilldown. Address is NOT in the Person data model the Angular client deserializes (consistent with Florida sheriff Marsy's Law / §119.071 suppression of victim/witness/inmate addresses) — confirmed by reading the SPA's Person class constructor, which holds: incarcerationId, inmateNumber, name, lastName, firstName, middleName, suffix, race, gender, weight, heightPrimary, heightSecondary, arrest[], bookingNumber, arrestingAgency, arrestType, overallBailAmount, nextCourtDate, courtLocation, courtDepartment, eyeColor, hairColor, bailDetails — no address/zip/DOB. Mugshot is fetched separately (jaxsheriff CDN, not part of the JSON row).

jso.exemptHandling: Source already suppresses exempt fields at the data-model level. This aligns with §119.071(2)(j)/(4)(d) (victim/witness redaction) and Marsy's Law Article I §16(b) of the FL Constitution. Charges, bond amount, booking date, mugshot are explicitly classified as public-record arrest information and are returned. NO marking/flagging of exempt rows is visible (they are simply not returned), so our scraper does not need to filter — what we receive is already the public-cleared payload.

For our freshness layer this is ideal: poll RecentBookings?timediff=2 every ~1 hour with 1-hour overlap for safety.

Three viable paths: (a) drive a real headed Playwright through the invisible checkbox once per session and cache the Authorization token (works for low-frequency polling but the token likely has a short TTL — 15-60 min typical); (b) use a paid captcha solver (2captcha ~$2.99/1000) at ~$0.003 per session, well under the hourly budget; (c) approach JSO PIO under §119.01 for a daily roster feed (preferred long-term).
Bright Data Web Unlocker DOES advertise reCAPTCHA solving as a feature on its premium tier — worth testing before paying 2captcha separately.
API uses non-standard port :8443 — some corp egress firewalls block non-443 HTTPS. Confirm Bright Data / Railway egress allows :8443.

The Person model has NO unique key besides incarcerationId — that's our PK. inmateNumber is per-individual (recidivism stable), bookingNumber is per-booking, incarcerationId is per-row. Use (incarcerationId, source) as ParcelSale-style upsert key.

HCSO Arrest Inquiry is an ASP.NET Core MVC app (IIS 10) at https://webapps.hcso.tampa.fl.us/arrestinquiry that is **hard-gated by Google reCAPTCHA v2** on every search submission. There is no public "today's bookings" list URL — the only way to retrieve any booking record is to POST the search form with a valid `g-recaptcha-response` token plus a hidden `__RequestVerificationToken` antiforgery field. Direct fetch and stealth-Chromium both reach the form page fine (HTTP 200, no Cloudflare/Akamai/rate-limit edge), but POSTing without solving the captcha returns the same form with `
  • Captcha validation has failed.
    • ` in the validation summary. Notice text on the page confirms a documented 30-minute refresh cadence, a 24-hour delay before new arrests appear in general listings (they ARE searchable by name during that window), and 90-day retention after release for public viewers. The source self-suppresses §119.071-exempt records: sealed/expunged arrests are excluded entirely, and the FDLE seal/expunge link is published on the notice. Result schema (column headers found in the form labels and the public notice) covers: Booking #, Name, Booking Date, Release Date, Race, Sex, DOB, and (when `SearchIncludeDetails=true` is checked) charges, bond amounts, and booking photo/mugshot. Building a freshness scraper here requires a captcha-solving budget (2Captcha / Anti-Captcha) — without that, the site is essentially closed to automation. This makes HCSO the highest-friction of the FL top-5 metros for jail-roster ingestion.

Source ALSO time-limits public visibility: records are removed 90 days after release date for unauthenticated viewers (only authorized law-enforcement / bond-industry / accredited-media accounts see full history). This means a freshness-layer scraper here captures a rolling 90-day window only.
risks: reCAPTCHA v2 site-key 6LcK1HopAAAAAEZgVeXqiN2_4zp6cQwRRXfc3uKJ blocks every search — requires paid CAPTCHA solver (2Captcha / Anti-Captcha at ~$2-3 per 1k solves, projected ~$0.05/day at 1 search/30min cadence)
AspNetCore antiforgery token has short server-side lifetime (~20 min default); must refresh GET+token before each POST batch
90-day visibility window means scraper cannot backfill history past 90 days post-release without authorized access
24h delay on general listings means D-0 data is name-only addressable — must use a planned-cohort sweep approach for true freshness
Authorized-access path exists but is gated by manual email approval (LE / bond industry / accredited media only) — not a viable automation route
ToS / robots.txt unchecked in probe — must verify before going live; ASP.NET app likely doesn't expose machine-readable robots policy, increasing yellow-zone risk posture
No rate-limit headers means failure mode for over-querying is unknown (could be silent IP block by IIS or app)
Single point of failure: only one search URL — no JSON API endpoint discovered, no XHR fallback

ocfl.summary: OCFL's BestJail roster is the easiest yellow-zone bond/jail target we've probed: ASP.NET MVC app with THREE clean JSON AJAX endpoints (getInmates, getInmateDetails, getCharges) plus a static daily-booking PDF. Direct HTTP with realistic Chrome UA returns 200s; no Cloudflare/Akamai/captcha, only Citrix NetScaler in front of IIS 10 (potential WAF-layer rate limiting but no challenge during the 5-request probe). The detail JSON exposes FULL street address + city + state + ZIP per inmate — exceptionally high signal value for distress cross-reference. SSN field is present but always blank (source-side §119.071 suppression). Mugshot included as base64 PNG. Bond amount and per-charge data are first-class fields. The /BestJail/PDF/bookings.pdf endpoint is the canonical 24-hour enumeration surface (no search gate needed); refresh cadence is documented at 30 min for the live AJAX surface. Build effort minimal — no clerk-style multi-step forms, no Kendo grid reverse-engineering, just three POSTs per booking.

accessibility.rateLimitObserved: n/a — no rate-limit headers seen during 5-request probe; Citrix NetScaler in front of IIS 10 may rate-limit at WAF layer, posture unknown

ocfl.exemptHandling: Source-side suppression: SSN field is present in the JSON schema but ALWAYS returned as empty string — server suppresses before sending. Juveniles do not appear (adult corrections facility only). DOB is NOT exposed — only AGE in the `BIRTH` field (mislabeled). Full home street address IS exposed (no address suppression), which is unusual permissive posture vs other FL sheriffs but matches Chapter 119's default "open" stance for non-exempt records. No visible marker for §119.071 exempt persons (LE officers, judges, etc.) — if they exist in the data the site simply omits them.
ocfl.paginationModel: No pagination. getInmates returns ALL current incarcerees matching the last-name prefix in a single JSON array (e.g. "SMITH" returned 29 rows in one response, 1921 bytes). For enumeration of the FULL current population, two viable strategies: (a) fetch /BestJail/PDF/bookings.pdf once per 24h cycle and parse it for the daily booking list (cleanest); (b) enumerate the AJAX endpoint with single-letter A..Z prefixes (26 calls covers entire roster). Strategy (a) is preferred because it matches the source's documented data-publication model and avoids brute-force enumeration that NetScaler might rate-limit.
ocfl.refreshCadence: Documented 30 min for the live AJAX surface (quoted verbatim on the page: "This information is updated every 30 minutes."). The daily-booking PDF is a separate artifact regenerated each midnight covering the preceding 24-hour window.
ocfl.sampleRowParseStrategy: No HTML parsing. Three JSON endpoints; consume directly. (1) Enumerate: GET /BestJail/PDF/bookings.pdf once per 24h, extract bookingNumbers via pdf-parse or similar (PDF 1.7, ~15 pages, ~150-250 rows expected). Diff against `JailBooking.unique(countyFips=12095, bookingNumber)` to find new bookings. (2) For each new bookingNumber, POST {body: "id="} to /BestJail/Home/getInmateDetails/{bookingNumber} → array length 1 → map: BOOKING→bookingNumber, NAME→fullName (parse "LAST, FIRST MIDDLE [SUFFIX]" pattern with comma split), RACE→race, GENDER→gender, BIRTH→age (NOT dob — string of years), DATEBOOKED+TIMEBOOKED→bookingDateTime (combine MM/DD/YYYY + HH:MMAM/PM), STREET+APTNUM+CITY+STATE+ZIPCODE.trim()→address fields, IMAGE→mugshotBase64 (store as bytes), HasImmigrationHold→holdFlag, CELL→cellLocation, HOLDS→holdsCount. (3) For each booking POST /BestJail/Home/getCharges/{bookingNumber} → array of N charges → map each: Charge→chargeDescription, BondAmount→parseFloat($)→bondAmountCents, CaseStatus→caseStatus (enum: PRESENTENCED|SENTENCED|PRETRIAL|...), ArrestingAgency→arrestingAgency, CourtCaseNumber→courtCaseNumber, CourtLocation→courtLocation, CaseSequence→caseSequence. Required POST headers: Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, Referer: https://netapps.ocfl.net/BestJail/Home/Inmates. Body literal: "id=" (empty value, ASP.NET MVC ignores it but the action expects a form POST). Schema notes for downstream: bookingNumber is a string with year-prefix (24/25/26 = 2024/25/26); ZIPCODE is right-padded with spaces — always trim(); IMAGE is base64-encoded PNG ~50-66KB so store as binary not base64 if going to PG.
risks: Citrix NetScaler in front of IIS may apply per-IP rate limiting at the WAF layer — posture unknown from a 5-request probe. Production cadence (1 PDF/30min + ~150 detail+charges enrichments/day) should stay well under any reasonable threshold, but use Bright Data residential proxy on detail-enrichment calls to distribute load across IPs.

The detail JSON exposes full home street address (STREET + APTNUM + CITY + ZIP). While this is public per Chapter 119, storing and exposing it in our product needs to thread §119.071 compliance carefully — if FL DOC or sheriff later flags a specific person as exempt, we MUST honor takedown requests within our policy window. Our DB schema should support a `suppressed` flag per record.

Mugshot is delivered as base64-encoded PNG embedded in the JSON detail response (~50-66KB each). At ~175 bookings/day this is ~10MB/day of image bytes. Store as binary in object storage (S3/R2), not as JSON column, and consider whether the product actually needs the mugshot — distress signal is the booking event, not the photo.

Booking number prefix encodes year (24/25/26). If the system ever wraps or changes format (unlikely but possible), our `JailBooking.unique(countyFips, bookingNumber)` constraint stays correct, but our year-inference logic would silently break — extract booking year from DATEBOOKED, not from prefix.

The getInmates list endpoint accepts an arbitrary last-name prefix path-param, returning all matching current inmates. A bad-faith actor could enumerate A..Z in 26 requests to dump the entire current roster. We must NOT enumerate this way ourselves (NetScaler may rate-limit OR flag it as abuse). Use the PDF for enumeration; use the AJAX endpoints only for keyed lookups of bookingNumbers we already know.
ZIPCODE field is right-padded with whitespace (e.g. '32818         '). Always trim() before storing or joining to property tables — silent join failures otherwise.

Site is currently jQuery 3.5.1 + Bootstrap 3 + ASP.NET MVC 5.2 — last meaningful update probably 2-3 years ago. Endpoints are stable but if the county ever modernizes, our scraper breaks fast. Build with a health-check that alerts on any non-200 or schema-drift (missing keys in detail JSON).

bso.summary: BSO's public arrest roster lives at https://apps.sheriff.org/arrestsearch — an AngularJS SPA on ASP.NET MVC 5.2 / IIS 10. Direct fetch returns IIS 200 with a vanilla User-Agent — no Cloudflare/Akamai, no JS challenge, no rate-limit headers. BUT the only path to row-level data is the POST endpoint /ArrestSearch/ArrestSearchJ which (a) requires ≥2 letters of first OR last name and (b) requires a valid Google reCAPTCHA v2 token in the `d` field of the JSON body. Server short-circuits with the bare string `"captcha"` if `d` is empty/invalid. There is NO "list all bookings today" view. The companion GET /ArrestSearch/GetUpdateTime is open (no captcha) and returns the data-pipeline freshness timestamp + helper URLs — useful as a cheap "did the roster tick?" poller. Documented refresh: every 15 minutes (confirmed in the results-panel HTML). Build strategy will be: poll GetUpdateTime to detect a refresh, then sweep [Aa-Zz] surname prefixes through ArrestSearchJ using a captcha-solving service (2Captcha/Anti-Captcha at ~$2/1000 solves; ~26-100 solves per full sweep). Detail-row enrichment via GET /ArrestSearch/InmateDetail/{JMS_NUMBER} — schema of that page NOT probed (would require a real JMS number; defer to Phase-2 scraper build with a single captcha-solved seed search).

accessibility.rateLimitObserved: none observed at HTTP layer — wall is reCAPTCHA v2 application-level, not edge

bso.paginationModel: Client-side only — results render via Angular `st-table` directive (smart-table) with `itemsByPage=15` controlling display, but ALL rows for a given (fn,ln) prefix come back in the single POST /ArrestSearch/ArrestSearchJ response as a flat JSON array (`vm.arrests`). No server-side pagination, no page=N URL param, no infinite scroll. Iteration model is name-prefix-based, not date-range or page-based.
bso.refreshCadence: 15 minutes — documented verbatim on the results page: "Returns are updated every 15 minutes. This information is current as of {{vm.updTime|date:'MM/dd/yyyy hh:mm a'}}". Confirmed via /ArrestSearch/GetUpdateTime JSON endpoint which exposes the last-pipeline-tick as ASP.NET `/Date(epoch_ms)/` format and is unauthenticated (no captcha).
bso.exemptHandling: Not directly observable without a captcha-solved search. The §119.071 exempt handling posture cannot be confirmed from the recon-phase artifacts. The "Disclaimer" text on the page covers accuracy/currency only and makes no statement about exemption suppression. Working assumption (verify in Phase-2 with a seed search): BSO follows the FDLE/sheriff convention of leaving most arrest records visible but suppressing per-person on legal request. Will need policy review once we see live rows. Site-side default appears to be "leave visible until told otherwise."
bso.sampleRowParseStrategy: Two layers must be parsed. LAYER 1 (search results — flat JSON from POST /ArrestSearch/ArrestSearchJ): server returns an array of objects with at least these fields confirmed from the Angular template: `JMS_NUMBER` (string — the booking ID, also used as `/ArrestSearch/InmateDetail/{JMS_NUMBER}` slug), `LAST_NAME`, `FIRST_NAME`, `MIDDLE_NAME`, `SEX`, and `LOCATION` (jail facility, e.g. "MAIN JAIL"). No DOB, charges, bond, or booking date in the search-list payload. Parse strategy: `const rows = await response.json(); for (const r of rows) emit({ jmsNumber: r.JMS_NUMBER, lastName: r.LAST_NAME, firstName: r.FIRST_NAME, middleName: r.MIDDLE_NAME, sex: r.SEX, location: r.LOCATION });`. LAYER 2 (per-inmate detail enrichment — server-rendered HTML from GET /ArrestSearch/InmateDetail/{JMS_NUMBER}): NOT probed in this recon (would require a real JMS we don't have, and surfacing a stranger's record without need is bad form). Expected to contain DOB, booking date, charges array, bond amount/type, mugshot URL, address — confirm structure in Phase-2 with a seed search. Selectors will likely be table-based since the landing page is bootstrap-styled MVC; will need stealth-chromium only if the detail page is also Angular-rendered (unconfirmed). Iteration driver: for each refresh tick (detected via /GetUpdateTime epoch advance), sweep surname prefixes ['aa','ab',...,'zz'] or single-letter ['a','b',...,'z'] through ArrestSearchJ — single-letter sweep = 26 captcha solves per refresh window; pair sweep = 676 solves (use only for catching long-tail). Recommend single-letter sweep every 15-30 min + GetUpdateTime gate to avoid hammering on stale data.
risks: reCAPTCHA v2 visual challenge required on EVERY search submission — operational cost ~$2/1000 solves via 2Captcha; ~26 solves per 15-min cycle = ~$0.05/day per BSO sweep
No 'list all' endpoint — must drive iteration via name-prefix sweeps; some bookings may be missed if a prefix returns >250 rows (unconfirmed result cap) within a single response
ASP.NET session cookie (ASP.NET_SessionId, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) is issued on landing — may need to carry across the POST or may be safe to drop; not yet confirmed
InmateDetail/{JMS_NUMBER} schema unknown — Phase-2 must probe ONE detail page after a captcha-solved seed search to lock the per-inmate parse (DOB, charges, bond, mugshot)
Possible silent rate limit / IP block at IIS layer not exposed via response headers — recon used only 4 requests so cannot rule out; mitigate with BD US-residential proxy rotation in production
§119.071 exempt posture unverified — Phase-2 must check whether BSO marks/suppresses exempt records or leaves them visible (drives our downstream policy)

Site is a 2010s-era ASP.NET MVC + AngularJS stack — likely to be replaced/redesigned at some point; the JS-controller endpoint contract (/ArrestSearch/ArrestSearchJ) is brittle to that kind of overhaul
Application Insights / WAF telemetry not visible to us — but BSO IT could add behavioural blocking at any time without notice

mdcr.summary: Miami-Dade Corrections (MDCR) Inmate Search is a search-only ASP.NET WebForms + DevExpress app (no public roster, no date browser). It requires Last Name (>=3 chars) + First Name (>=3 chars) and is protected by reCAPTCHA Enterprise v3 in INVISIBLE mode (action='search', site key 6LeMreYsAAAAABiQ8y8CSG41sZQ0eHO7DmGvml4d). Cloudflare fronts the site but returns cf-cache-status=DYNAMIC (not actively challenging). Stealth-chromium passes both Cloudflare AND grecaptcha-enterprise.execute() silently on the first try, no proxy needed — confirmed with one live SMITH/JOHN search that returned a valid result row. Each result row exposes 13 columns (JailNumber, BookingName, BookingDate, Race, Sex, DOB, Hair, Eye, Weight, Height, IDS, Location, MugLink) plus a separately-rendered detail row containing one or more Warrant Cases with Charges and Bond ('NO BOND' or dollar amount). To enumerate the entire ~6,500-inmate Miami-Dade population we must iterate a surname dictionary; per-row HTML is bulk and self-contained so we can capture full case/charge/bond data in one request per surname pair. No address/zip in results (suppressed at source). Daily booking volume estimate: ~150-200/day (Miami-Dade is the third-largest US jail system, average daily population ~6,500-7,000 with ~14% bi-weekly churn, per published MDCR statistics).

accessibility.rateLimitObserved: n/a — no headers seen; site is small (~6.5k records) and search-only; cadence should be self-imposed at <=1 req/3s to be polite

mdcr.sampleRowParseStrategy:
Each search returns a DevExpress BootstrapGridView whose data rows match selector 'tr.dxgvDataRow_Metropolis' (or generic 'table.dxbs-gridview tbody tr.dxgvDataRow'). Within a data row, the columns are positionally ordered as: td[0]=mugshot (parse img.src — pattern https://wwwx.miamidade.gov/apps/mdcr/correctionsmug/{token}.JPG; empty if no mug on file), td[1]=JailNumber (9-digit string, e.g. '260137845' — this is the unique bookingId), td[2]=BookingName ('LAST, FIRST [MIDDLE]' — split on ', '), td[3]=BookingDate ('MM/DD/YYYY HH:mm' 24-hr — parse as America/New_York), td[4]=Race (single letter: B/W/H/A/I/U), td[5]=Sex (M/F), td[6]=DOB ('MM/DD/YYYY'), td[7]=Hair (3-char code: BLK/BRO/BLN/GRY/RED/BAL/UNK), td[8]=Eye (3-char code: BRO/BLU/GRN/HZL/GRY/UNK), td[9]=Weight ('### Lbs'), td[10]=Height ('F\\' I\"' — note double-space between feet and inches), td[11]=IDS (7-digit internal person ID — links bookings to the same person across multiple incarcerations), td[12]=Location (facility code: TGKCC=Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center, PDC=Pre-Trial Detention Center, MWCC=Metro West Detention Center, etc.). IMMEDIATELY AFTER each data row sits a sibling 'tr.dxgvDetailRow' (or 'tr' with a td[colspan=13] containing 'Case(s) Information'). Inside that detail td the structure is flat HTML separated by
with bold labels. Parse with regex: for each /Warrant Case:<\\/strong>\\s*([A-Z0-9]+)\\s*<\\/l>\\s*Desc:\\s*<\\/strong>\\s*([^<]+?)\\s*Bond:\\s*<\\/strong>\\s*([^<]+?)\\s*Charge:\\s*<\\/strong>\\s*([^<]+?)=3, first>=3) pairs).
mdcr.paginationModel: DevExpress callback pagination via Content_BootstrapGridView1 (page size 10 default, selectable 10/20/50). Page summary 'Page X of Y (N items)' rendered in .dxbs-pager .summary div. Each page change is a __doPostBack with updated __VIEWSTATE — cheaper to bump page size to 50 once and iterate fewer pages. NO date-range filter exists; the only enumeration knob is the search form (LastName + FirstName, both >= 3 chars).
mdcr.refreshCadence: No documented cadence. Recommend internal poll cadence of 4-6h per surname slice (jail-system data churns on booking/release events, but the site is search-only so we cannot detect 'new bookings' without re-running the dictionary). For real-time freshness layer: prioritize a 'recent bookings' synthetic feed by iterating the top-200 most-common US surnames every 2h (covers ~40-50% of population, ~6 hits/run = ~72 hits/day total — well within polite).
mdcr.exemptHandling: The MDCR site appears to leave §119.071-exempt records visible by default (the public terminal exposes name + DOB + booking date + charges + bond + mugshot for the inmate we sampled). No 'exempt' marker, no redaction icon, no suppression notice visible in the result HTML. Florida statute §119.071(4)(d) lets specific categories (LEOs, judges, prosecutors, victims of certain crimes, etc.) request suppression individually — those records are presumably filtered server-side and simply don't appear in results, leaving us no signal to detect them. Our policy posture: assume the site has already applied statutory suppression, treat everything we receive as publishable, but apply our own §119.071 sensitive-occupation filter as defense-in-depth before surfacing to users.
risks: reCAPTCHA Enterprise Invisible — stealth-chromium passed on first try with no proxy, but Google can tighten v3 scoring at any time. If score drops below the site's threshold the form will silently fail (gmsg='Security verification failed'). Mitigation: detect '#Content_gmsg' non-empty after submit, fall back to BD residential proxy + retry; if still failing, switch hdnRecaptchaMode='Checkbox' path (the JS code supports both modes, suggesting MDCR has a fallback).

Search-only interface forces surname-dictionary enumeration — incomplete coverage (top-1000 US surnames ≈ 70% of population, top-5000 ≈ 90%). Missed bookings = missed distress signals. Mitigation: combine US Census Hispanic-surname list (Miami-Dade is 68% Hispanic — different name distribution than US average) + dynamic dictionary expansion from the IDS field (track recurring surnames we discover).

Cloudflare currently returns DYNAMIC but could escalate to JS challenge or Turnstile if our traffic pattern looks botlike. Mitigation: keep per-source concurrency <=1, randomize 3-8s between requests, rotate stealth UA across runs.
ASP.NET __VIEWSTATE is required for every postback — invalidates after ~30 min. Mitigation: re-fetch landing page at start of every batch (one warmup hit per scrape session).

Detail row HTML uses inline styles and bold-label/br-separator formatting that could break on site redesign. Mitigation: parser must be tolerant of whitespace and label-case variations; cover with snapshot test that re-runs against a saved 'gold' HTML fixture.

Mugshot URLs are hosted on wwwx.miamidade.gov (separate hostname from app) — fetching them is technically a second cross-host request per inmate; downloading may be rate-limited differently. Mitigation: defer mugshot fetch to a separate worker queue, throttle independently.

pbso.summary: PBSO publishes its booking blotter at https://www3.pbso.org/blotter/ (a ColdFusion app on a separate subdomain, NOT the menu page at pbso.org/arrest-jail_menu). The blotter is a SEARCH FORM — POST to /blotter/searchresults.cfm with start_date / end_date returns up to 5 inmate records per page with pagination ('Page 1 of N', 'Last »'). A 1-day window (05/30→05/31/2026) returned 55 bookings (~50-70/day average for the county). Each record exposes: Name, Race, Gender, Facility, OBTS Number, Booking Date/Time, Cell Location, Arresting Agency, Release Date (N/A while in custody), Holds For Other Agencies, Jacket Number, Booking Number, and 1+ Charges (statute code + description + Original Bond + Current Bond). DOB, address/zip, and mugshot are NOT in this feed — PBSO redacts those at source. hCaptcha is LOADED on the landing page but does NOT gate the form submit — stealth-chromium POSTs through cleanly without solving a challenge. Scraper pattern: stealth-chromium navigate → fill start/end → click submit → loop pages 1..N parsing flowing div text into records bounded by 'Name:' anchors.

accessibility.rateLimitObserved: none observed in probe; ColdFusion CFID/CFTOKEN session cookies issued — keep concurrency = 1 and jitter 3-5s between page clicks to avoid session throttling

pbso.exemptHandling: PBSO suppresses DOB / address / mugshot at the source — the blotter only returns Name, Race, Gender, OBTS, Booking #, Jacket #, Charges, Bond, Facility, Cell Location, Arresting Agency. This is a self-imposed minimization (typical Florida sheriff posture). We did NOT see any 'EXEMPT' / 'CONFIDENTIAL' placeholder rows — the site appears to filter §119.071 protected-class bookings (LEO / victim / juvenile) out of the result set entirely rather than render redacted shells. Our scraper inherits the suppression — there is no §119.071 leakage risk from this source. However, the scraper should still defensively flag any record whose Name field contains 'JUVENILE', 'EXEMPT', or 'CONFIDENTIAL' and route to quarantine, in case PBSO's filtering ever leaks.
pbso.paginationModel: Form-driven server-side pagination. Result page shows 5 records and advertises 'Page 1 of N' (we saw 'Page 1 of 11' for 55 matches across one day). Pagination links stay on /blotter/searchresults.cfm; the page number is almost certainly a hidden form field or query param re-POSTed. To iterate: follow the numeric page links in DOM (`page.click('a:has-text("Next")')` or numeric links) — was out of scope for the gentle 5-request probe budget to confirm the exact param name. Date range is the primary slicer — scraper should sweep with start_date=2d-ago & end_date=today daily, then page 1..N.
pbso.sampleRowParseStrategy: Each inmate record is rendered as flowing div content (NOT a <table> — page.evaluate found 0 tables on the result page). Records are separated by repeating 'Name:' labels. PARSE STRATEGY: (1) extract the full result-page innerText via page.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText); (2) split on /\bName:\s+/ — each chunk after the first is one inmate; (3) within each chunk extract via line-anchored regexes on the multi-line text: name = first line; then /^Race:\s*(.+)$/m, /^Gender:\s*(.+)$/m, /^Facility:\s*(.+)$/m, /^OBTS Number:\s*(\d+)$/m, /^Booking Date\/Time:\s*([\d\/]+\s+[\d:]+)$/m, /^Cell Location:\s*(.+)$/m, /^Arresting Agency:\s*(.+)$/m, /^Release Date:\s*(.+)$/m, /^Holds For Other Agencies:\s*(.+)$/m, /^Jacket Number:\s*(\d+)$/m, /^Booking Number:\s*(\d+)$/m. (4) Charges block starts at /^Charges$/m — every subsequent quadruple of lines is one charge: line1 = statute code with class suffix in parens (e.g. '784.041 2A (FT)' — FT=felony 3rd, MF=misdemeanor 1st, MS=misdemeanor 2nd), line2 = description, line3 = 'Original Bond: $X.XX', line4 = 'Current Bond: $X.XX Bond Information'. Charge block ends at the next 'Name:' anchor or end of page. Primary key for dedupe: Booking Number (e.g. 2026014341) — county-scoped, monotonic, present on every record. OBTS Number is also unique and statewide and a better cross-county key. ALTERNATIVE structural parse: try `await page.locator('text=Name:').all()` and then `.locator('..').textContent()` to chunk by DOM siblings — only fall back to regex if the DOM doesn't expose a per-record container.
risks: hCaptcha script + logo are present on the landing page — currently NOT enforced on form submit, but PBSO can toggle gating at any time. Build the scraper with a 'captcha-detected → halt + alert ops' branch, not silent retry.

ColdFusion session cookies (CFID/CFTOKEN) are issued; if we hammer in parallel, the site may session-throttle or 500. Hard cap to 1 concurrent session per scrape run and jitter 3-5s between page clicks.

No table markup — schema is purely visual / DOM-flow text. A site-wide redesign or label tweak (e.g. 'Cell Location:' becoming 'Location:') would silently break the parser. Add field-presence assertions + alert when <90% of records yield a Booking Number.

Only 5 records per result page → 55 bookings = 11 page-clicks for ONE day. For a 7-day backfill we're looking at ~70-90 page-clicks per run. Stay well under hourly request burst; spread across ~10-15 min with jitter.

DOB is NOT present in the feed — entity resolution against our Parcel/Person tables must rely on (name + city of arrest + booking date) which has higher false-match risk than (name + DOB). Plan to skip-trace via BatchData before linking the bond signal to a property/owner.

PBSO does NOT publish mugshots in this feed (deliberate § restriction). We should NOT scrape mugshots from any secondary source — keep the scraper text-only to honor the source's minimization posture.

schemaDesign.normalizedNameSpec:
CANONICAL normalizeInmateName(raw: string): string

PURPOSE: produce a deterministic, comparison-safe key for fuzzy join against
Parcel.ownerName (which is bulk-roll-derived and equally messy).

STEPS (in order — DO NOT reorder):
  1. Trim leading/trailing whitespace.
  2. Uppercase ASCII (raw.toUpperCase()).
  3. Unicode NFD-normalize and strip combining marks so "JOSÉ" → "JOSE",
     "PEÑA" → "PENA".
  4. If string contains a comma, split on the FIRST comma — left side is
     last name, right side is "first middle suffix". Rejoin as
     "<first middle suffix> <last>". (HCSO/MDCR/PBSO ship "LAST, FIRST MIDDLE";
     OCFL ships "LAST, FIRST MIDDLE [SUFFIX]"; JSO/BSO ship separate fields.)
  5. Replace all punctuation [.,'`"’\-()/\\] with single space.
  6. Collapse runs of whitespace to a single space.
  7. Strip the following SUFFIXES off the END of the token list, repeatedly
     until none match (case-insensitive after step 2; matching is whole-token):
       JR, SR, II, III, IV, V, VI, ESQ, MD, DDS, PHD,
       LIFE ESTATE, LIFE ESTATES, LIFE EST, LIFE-EST, L/E, LE,
       TRUSTEE, TRUSTEES, TRS, TR, TTEE, TTEES,
       REVOCABLE TRUST, FAMILY TRUST, LIVING TRUST, TRUST, EST, ESTATE,
       DECEASED, DEC'D, DECD,
       ET AL, ETAL, ET UX, ETUX, ET VIR, ETVIR
     Multi-word suffixes match GREEDILY (e.g. "LIFE ESTATE" before "ESTATE").
  8. Strip leading articles: "A ", "THE ".
  9. Final trim + single-space collapse.

EXAMPLES (input → output):
  "SMITH, JOHNNIE"                          → "JOHNNIE SMITH"
  "SMITH, JASON EUGENE "                    → "JASON EUGENE SMITH"
  "BLACKMON, TYLER PATRICK"                 → "TYLER PATRICK BLACKMON"
  "STEVENS, JUSTIN EDWARD"                  → "JUSTIN EDWARD STEVENS"
  "Garcia-Lopez, José Manuel Jr."           → "JOSE MANUEL GARCIA LOPEZ"
  "O'Brien, Patrick III"                    → "PATRICK O BRIEN"
  "SMITH JOHN A LIFE ESTATE"                → "JOHN A SMITH"
  "JONES MARY ET AL"                        → "MARY JONES"
  "DOE JANE TRUSTEE"                        → "JANE DOE"
  "DOE JOHN & JANE LIVING TRUST"            → "JOHN JANE DOE"   (& replaced with space at step 5)
  "  WILLIAMS,  ROBERT   E   JR  "          → "ROBERT E WILLIAMS"
  "PEÑA, ANA-MARÍA"                         → "ANA MARIA PENA"

NULL/EMPTY HANDLING:
  - Empty string in → empty string out (caller should treat as "no name match").
  - Single token in (e.g. "DOE") → "DOE" (no comma reorder).

IDEMPOTENT: normalizeInmateName(normalizeInmateName(x)) === normalizeInmateName(x).

DETERMINISTIC: pure function, no I/O, no Date.now(), safe to call inside

bondTypeTaxonomy.meaning: Held without bond. JSO 'NO BOND', OCFL bond=0 AND case shows pretrial/held flag, MDCR detail row literal 'NO BOND', PBSO Current Bond $0.00 with no Original Bond either. Strong distress signal: defendant cannot bail out.
Cash-only bond required by court. Where source distinguishes (JSO bailDetails.bondType, MDCR Warrant Desc 'CASH'). Not a default — only set when sheriff explicitly tags it.

Bondsman / surety bond allowed. The default when a dollar amount is published and no other type is specified (covers OCFL bondAmount > 0, PBSO Current Bond > 0, BSO detail). Implied unless overridden.
Released on own recognizance. PBSO arresting agency notes / JSO releaseLog when bond=0 AND release recorded same day. Match heuristically; flag for review.
Signature bond / personal recognizance with promise to appear. JSO bailDetails distinguishes from ROR in some statutes; group with ROR for downstream analytics if not differentiated.
Real-property pledge bond. Rare across all 6 sources; JSO bailDetails sometimes carries 'Property'. Capture when present, do not map other types here.

Multi-charge booking where charges carry DIFFERENT bond types (e.g. one no_bond hold + one surety). Use when count(distinct bondType across charges) > 1. Downstream UI should expand to per-charge view.
Detainer / immigration hold / out-of-county warrant — defendant not bondable until hold cleared. OCFL HasImmigrationHold=true, PBSO 'Holds For Other Agencies' = Yes, MDCR 'ALIAS CAPIAS' descriptions.
Already sentenced — no bond applicable. OCFL CaseStatus='SENTENCED'/'PRESENTENCED' with NO BOND. Excludes from distress-signal scoring (already-convicted, not a deal trigger).
Bond data present but bondType cannot be inferred. Fallback bucket. Should NEVER be the majority case — alert if >5% of weekly rows hit this.

schemaDesign.additionalModelsNeeded:
No separate Charge or Mugshot table is needed for the v1 build.

REASONING (Charge):
- Charges are stored as Json on InmateBooking with the shape:
    [{ statute: string, description: string, severity: string|null,
       bondAmount: number|null,   // cents
       bondType: string|null,     // normalized via bondTypeTaxonomy
       caseNumber: string|null,
       caseStatus: string|null,   // OCFL CaseStatus, MDCR Charge Satisfied
       arrestingAgency: string|null,
       courtCaseNumber: string|null,
       warrantCaseId: string|null,
       sequence: number }]
- Three denormalized columns on InmateBooking (chargeCount, topChargeStatute,
  totalBond/highestSingleBond) cover 95% of query patterns (filter by bond
  range, filter by top-charge family, "show me felony bookings only").
- Row volume: ~600 bookings/day across 6 sheriffs × ~2 charges avg = ~1,200
  charge rows/day. Over a year that's ~440K. Not enough to justify a second
  table's join cost vs JSON path queries in PG.
- If a future ML need requires per-charge filtering on statute family across
  millions of rows, we can promote to a Charge model later via a one-shot
  Json-fan-out backfill; the unique key (sheriffSlug, bookingId) makes that
  safe.

REASONING (Mugshot):
- Mugshots are binary blobs (OCFL ships ~66KB base64 PNG; MDCR/JSO/HCSO are
  CDN URLs). PG is the wrong place for either. We store them in R2/S3 keyed
  by `jail-mugshots/{sheriffSlug}/{bookingId}.jpg` and put the storage key
  + the original source URL on InmateBooking. No extra model needed.

REASONING (BookingRelease event log):
- Could add a JailReleaseEvent table to track release-date transitions as
  time-series (mirrors Foreclosure stage transitions). NOT needed for v1
  because most sources only flip releaseDate ONCE; the JSO ReleaseLog endpoint
  is the only one that benefits, and we can model it as an UPDATE on the
  matching InmateBooking row keyed by (sheriffSlug, bookingId).
- Defer to v2 if release-event-driven analytics emerge.

REASONING (existing models we DO link to):
- RawSnapshot — keep the full JSON payload of every scrape there (entityType
  = "inmate_booking", sourceTag matches InmateBooking.sourceTag). InmateBooking
  carries the optional rawSnapshotId pointer.
- BulkIngestJob — every scraper run for a sheriff writes one row here with
  sourceKey FK to ScrapeRegistry. Reuse the existing audit pipe.
- ScrapeRegistry — register 6 new rows (jso-bookings, hcso-bookings,
  ocfl-bestjail, bso-arrest-search, mdcr-inmate-search, pbso-blotter), all
  with legalRisk="yellow" per FL-COVERAGE-PLAN §5.1.
- Parcel — referenced via InmateBooking.parcelId (soft FK by the matcher).

        drift detection wipes.
     d. Confirm with `\d flipops."InmateBooking"` in psql that all 9

4. REGISTER the 6 scrapers in ScrapeRegistry (manual seed via tsx script —
   one row per sheriff):
     - sourceKey: jso-bookings, hcso-bookings, ocfl-bestjail,
       bso-arrest-search, mdcr-inmate-search, pbso-blotter
     - legalRisk: "yellow" (all 6, per FL-COVERAGE-PLAN §5.1 — captcha-gated
       or scraper-required sources)
     - strategy: "incremental-date" (JSO/PBSO/OCFL — time-windowed) or
       "snapshot-diff" (HCSO/BSO/MDCR — surname-sweep, diff against last run)
     - cronExpr varied per probe refreshCadence (JSO=hourly, OCFL=30min,

5. BACKFILL: not applicable — net-new entity, no historical data to migrate.

6. ROLLBACK plan:

7. DEPLOY ORDER:
     - Schema push first (zero-downtime — additive).
     - Then ship scrapers + matcher in separate PRs so a scraper bug never
